rationale: I read the complete held EO 8714 (6 FR 1517, Mar. 20, 1941, signed Mar. 18, 1941, [No. 8714]): three succession paragraphs designating, in order, the Fiscal Assistant Secretary, the senior Assistant Secretary on duty and the General Counsel to perform the duties of the Secretary of the Treasury during absence or sickness, plus a last paragraph revoking Executive Order No. 6202-B of July 11, 1933. It has no own term and no savings clause; the six machine TERM leads are only the 'until such absence or sickness shall cease' condition on each designation, not an ending. I read the held full text of EO 10586 (20 FR 361, Jan. 15, 1955, signed Jan. 13, 1955): it sets a new succession (Under Secretary for Monetary Affairs, Assistant Secretaries, General Counsel) and closes 'Executive Order No. 8714 of March 18, 1941, entitled "Designating Certain Officers To Act as Secretary of the Treasury in Case of Absence or Sickness of the Secretary", is hereby revoked.' That names EO 8714 by number, date and title, reaches all of it, and carries no exception or savings clause. D6 self-check: the only later event in the history is that revocation (OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 10586'; the 1989 snapshot row is empty). A text search of the held full-run Executive Order texts finds EO 8714 named only in EO 10586 and in the neighbouring-page extracts of EO 10587 and EO 10588, which carry the same page. EO 10586 was itself revoked by EO 10941 sec. 2 (held), a new Treasury succession order that does not mention EO 8714, so the revocation of the revoking order does not revive 8714. No amendment, extension or re-delegation of EO 8714 exists in the held texts, and no own term ran out earlier. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing Jan. 13, 1955, EO 10586 states no later date) is not otherwise adjudicated.
